page.group.strokes.hint: amplitude, and how even the reach is
page.group.stillness.hint: quiet passages hold flat instead of jittering
page.group.filler.hint: replace motion-free passages with a rhythm
page.stylehint.level: strokes ride the predicted level: steadier speed, less reach
page.stylehint.composed: the full decode: reach, holds, stillness handling, fast events
page.help.style.title: style
page.help.style.body:
composed writes the full production decode: stroke level from the level head, amplitude from the envelope, endpoints stretched to the band rails, holds parked by the dwell head, fast reversals from the event head.

level writes strokes riding the predicted level with the model's own travel: steadier speed and a simpler look, but less reach and no hold parking.

Holds and stillness apply to composed only; strokes, gap filler and device limits apply to both.
page.help.range.title: range
page.help.range.body: The written 0–100 positions are mapped linearly onto this span. For devices that should not reach their physical ends.
page.help.mspeed.title: max speed
page.help.mspeed.body: Caps how fast consecutive actions may move (position units per second), for hardware with a speed limit. 0 = no cap.
page.help.cutEase.title: seam speed
page.help.cutEase.body: This is the speed limit that cut smoothing uses, in position units per second. The decode removes the points at a cut only when the movement between them is faster than this value. A smaller value smooths more cuts, but it can also remove movement that the video shows. A larger value smooths fewer cuts. The default is 250.
page.help.intensity.title: intensity
page.help.intensity.body: Scales stroke amplitude about mid-range: 0.5 halves strokes, 2.0 doubles them (clipped at the ends). 1.0 = the model's own amplitude.
page.help.depth.title: depth uniformity
page.help.depth.body:
Lines up neighbouring tops (and bottoms) at a steady depth: each reversal is pulled toward the running MEDIAN of nearby same-direction reversals — the level that moves the points least, so matching neighbours stay put and the outlier comes to them.

off = the model's own reach; subtle / even / locked pull progressively harder.
page.help.depthKnob.title: depth numbers
page.help.depthKnob.body: The numbers behind the depth preset. dose blends between the model's reach (0) and full alignment (1). window is how far the median looks, in seconds: short = local, long = whole passage.
page.help.dwells.title: dwells
page.help.dwells.body: When the model is confident the scene holds a plateau, the draft parks at that level instead of sweeping through it. This sets how confident it must be: cautious parks only sure ones (safer on unfamiliar footage), eager parks more.
page.help.dwellsNum.title: dwell confidence
page.help.dwellsNum.body: The raw confidence bar (0..1) behind the dwells preset: a hold the model is this sure of starts being parked, and one it is fully sure of is parked at full strength. Lower it to park more, raise it to park only the certain ones. A value different from the preset's own number becomes the override the recipe echoes.
page.help.stillness.title: stillness
page.help.stillness.body: Near-still passages hold flat instead of minting tiny phantom strokes. low keeps micro-motion, high kills phantoms harder.
page.help.stillNum.title: still floor
page.help.stillNum.body:
The raw velocity floor (position units per second) behind the stillness preset: predicted motion below it counts as still.

The gap filler searches for gaps with this same floor, so raising it makes both trigger more.
page.help.fillerSel.title: gap filler
page.help.fillerSel.body:
Replaces passages the model calls motion-free with a configurable background rhythm instead of leaving them parked flat. Presets bundle gap, rate, amplitude and pattern; edit any number and the select shows custom.

Filled spans draw as the bright band at the top of the timeline.
page.help.fillGap.title: gap before filling
page.help.fillGap.body:
How many motion-free seconds before filler starts. 0 = off. Kept motion inside a gap pauses the count without resetting it, so a dead passage interrupted by a few real strokes still fills around them.

On busy footage keep this high: short quiet stretches there are usually the model losing track, not real dead time.
page.help.fillKnob.title: rhythm
page.help.fillKnob.body: The rhythm itself: speed in strokes per minute, and depth in position units above and below the held level.
page.help.fillModelW.title: model influence
page.help.fillModelW.body:
How much the model shapes a filled gap. At 1.0 confident motion inside a gap interrupts the rhythm, and the rhythm rides the model's level as it drifts. At 0.0 the gap is a pure artificial rhythm: nothing short interrupts it, and it sits at one steady level per gap (taken from where the gap starts and ends).

Slide down when filled passages feel twitchy or random; the model's misfires on dead footage stop reaching the script. Long motion (see replace garbage up to) always survives, at every setting.
page.help.fillReal.title: keep real motion
page.help.fillReal.body:
Motion inside a gap is kept only if it holds at least this speed (position units per second) for at least this much time in total. A single brief spike is not evidence — real strokes sustain their speed, hallucination bursts do not. Anything below the bar is garbage output and is replaced by the rhythm.

Kept motion interrupts the rhythm without cancelling the gap: filling resumes on the beat after it.

The model influence slider raises this bar further as it goes down.
page.help.fillBridge.title: replace garbage up to
page.help.fillBridge.body: Only motion SHORTER than this can be replaced as garbage. Anything longer always survives, however slow — a long slow passage is never overwritten — and ends the gap, so filling starts counting from zero after it.
page.help.fillRamp.title: seam fade
page.help.fillRamp.body: The cross-fade where filler meets real motion, seconds per side. 0 = one stroke.
page.help.fillSway.title: sway
page.help.fillSway.body: Slow, deterministic variation of the rhythm's amplitude so it does not read as a metronome: the fraction it varies by, and the period in seconds. The same clip always drafts the same.
page.help.fillPattern.title: pattern
page.help.fillPattern.body:
steady = continuous strokes for the whole gap.
burst = groups of strokes with rests between them, closer to how scripts are authored.
page.help.fillBurst.title: burst
page.help.fillBurst.body: Strokes per burst, and seconds of rest between bursts. Used only while pattern is burst.

page.help.cropShow.title: crop
page.help.cropShow.body:
This draft was cropped: instead of the whole frame, the goblins were shown one rect per shot, picked from where their attention actually sits. (It happens by default; --no-autocrop, or the picker's C, drafts the whole frame — and a clip whose attention wants the whole frame is left alone anyway, which is why this readout is not always here.) The overlay draws that rect on the frame and dims the rest, so you can see what they were looking at; C toggles it.

The reading next to it: the zoom the crop gained, how many shots were cropped, and esc — the share of sampled moments whose attention wandered outside its own rect, which is the number that says a crop was too tight.

Cropped shots also draw as the green band on the timeline, one span per shot.

The rect can also be yours: the crop page that opens before a draft lets you drag it onto the action, and what you drew there is what this overlay shows.
page.help.envSeed.title: variation
page.help.envSeed.body: The goblins select how deep each stroke goes. A different number makes them select differently, and gives a small variation of the same script. On one video, depths moved by 1 of 100 on average and 99% of the changes of direction stayed at the same time. Each number gives the same result every time. This takes longer than the other controls: the goblins must read the video again.
page.help.cutSmooth.title: cut smoothing
page.help.cutSmooth.body: At a cut in the video, the decode writes one point on each side of the cut. The two points are approximately one frame apart, so the device must make the full position change of the cut in that time. This feels like a jolt. When cut smoothing is on, the decode removes those points if the movement between them is too fast. The movement then runs from the last change of direction before the cut to the first change of direction after it, which is what a human writer does. The stroke keeps its full depth and no time changes.
